text:
Anaheim has handed Jackson LaCombe the keys. He is playing 26:37 a night, up from 24:15 last season, and he is on the ice for 82% of the Ducks' power-play time (65% before). The result is 25 points in 23 games, 24 of them assists and 16 on the power play, a jump from 0.71 points a game to 1.09.

The playmaking is real. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 98th percentile among defensemen for primary shot assists last season, and Evolving-Hockey ranked him 46th of 215 defensemen, with his team creating more with him on after adjustments (94th percentile).

The five-on-five numbers are the catch. With LaCombe on the ice, Anaheim has taken only 40% of the expected goals (the quality of chances), well below its rate without him, and the Ducks have scored 5.9 more goals than those chances deserve. His points rate also sits above the top of our talent range. The role and the power-play time are what make this a breakout; some of the scoring pace is bounces. We'd watch the even-strength share, which is what decides whether 26 minutes stays his number.
